The source Markdown contains no image references, so no visual asset or manifest was required.

The newest [[JoshuaSchachter]] source adds [[Delicious|Del.icio.us]] as both a product-origin case and a target-side acquisition case. A personal Unix link file with terse hash-marked notes became Muxway and then a multi-user service where low-friction tags supported retrieval, observation, and sharing; rapid traffic, frequent downtime, founder exhaustion, and weak second-round fundraising then made Yahoo's serious offer and promised indexing infrastructure attractive. New [[FounderExitTradeoff]] separates that ex ante decision from the ex post product outcome: Schachter treats financial stability as intellectually rational while describing lost momentum and control as emotionally costly. [[AcquisitionStrategy]] and [[Yahoo]] gain the post-close mechanism missing from broader strategy accounts—some technical help can coexist with unfulfilled resource promises, committee-delayed hardware, absent decision-guiding mission, and staff reallocation until an acquired product has little capacity left. The account is a retrospective founder interview without deal documents, Yahoo's response, independent operating metrics, or a counterfactual future; its US$30 million press figure is explicitly rejected, and its tagging-priority and product-influence claims remain unverified here. Both local image embeds were opened and omitted as duplicate non-evidentiary portraits.

The newest payments architecture source adds [[DistributedPaymentArchitecture]] as a correctness chain rather than a list of fashionable components. In the first-person [[Uber]] case, measurable availability, accuracy, capacity, and tail-latency targets frame the design; horizontal scaling and replication address capacity and node failure; payment initiation uses strong consistency while recent-transaction views can accept eventual consistency; and [[DataDurability]] plus [[DurableMessaging]] preserve acknowledged records and payment-intent work. Kafka's at-least-once delivery deliberately admits duplicate messages, so [[IdempotentPaymentProcessing]] uses versioning, optimistic locking, and a strongly consistent store to prevent duplicate charges or refunds. This supplies a positive boundary for [[DistributedSystemRestraint]] because the source describes both high load and severe correctness requirements, but the evidence remains one incomplete practitioner retrospective: it does not document topology, acknowledgements, incidents, reconciliation, security, compliance, or end-to-end loss measurements, and its broad “SLA,” “delivered once,” and distributed-locking terminology requires qualification. The decorative Earth photograph was omitted; two retained diagrams illustrate a surviving replica after one data-node failure and a surviving queued message after one broker-node failure without proving behavior under correlated failures.

The newest [[FredWilson]] source adds a household-balance-sheet boundary to the wiki's active-investing and technology-bubble material. Wilson says wealth accumulated during the 1996–2000 Internet boom remained concentrated in venture capital and Internet stocks, then fell roughly 90% after the bubble burst; two real-estate holdings bought earlier became the family's remaining net worth. [[AssetAllocation]] therefore gains an ex-ante survivability rule: diversification must exist before stress because investors may initially expect recovery, selling can continue, and individual public holdings can go to zero. Wilson's desired four-way mix of cash-like instruments, blue-chip stocks, low-leverage income real estate, and a high-risk bucket is a personal target rather than a universal allocation, as is his estimated 5% direct and fund-mediated crypto exposure. Read with [[TechnologyBubbles]], the durable synthesis is that conviction in an underlying technology does not justify allowing one speculative sector to dominate household wealth; partial profit-taking, taxes, liquidity, leverage limits, and cross-asset reallocation are complementary forms of capital preservation. The source is a short 2017 personal essay without audited holdings, counterfactual returns, or evidence that its weights fit other investors, and its Markdown contains no image references.

The newest CodeAhoy source adds [[SearchAssistedProgramming]] as the external-lookup layer of software expertise. Search can retrieve low-value-to-memorize details, expose candidate solutions, and challenge suspect reasoning across unfamiliar languages, frameworks, and APIs, but the useful capability is not query volume alone: it includes problem recognition, query formulation, source discrimination, contextual adaptation, and verification. The author's [[Netty]] example—23 Google searches during a 255-line Java client-and-server task, often reaching [[StackOverflow]], Netty's site, GitHub, and JavaDocs—shows how lookup can support real implementation without establishing a normal query rate or using lines of code as a quality measure. This complements [[SystematicLearning]] and [[DeveloperDocumentation]] rather than replacing them, because durable understanding is what lets a programmer detect stale, insecure, or context-mismatched results. The source is a short 2016 practitioner anecdote, not a study of expert behavior; it contains no image references, and its Einstein attribution is unsupported within the saved article.

The newest [[CollaborativeFund]] source adds [[PersonStrategyFit]] as a boundary on universal advice. A method can be sensible in general or successful for an institution yet suppress the individual voice, intuition, temperament, or skills that made a person effective; the essay's two anonymized independent-writer examples make that risk concrete without establishing causality. [[PersonalInvestorStrategy]] therefore gains a sustainability test beneath its diversified, low-cost, rules-based defaults: another person's investing style may be financially plausible but psychologically or ethically intolerable for the person copying it, while different spending choices need not rank as right and wrong. This aligns with [[WantRealityCareerFramework]] by separating authentic wants from borrowed goals and makes personal benchmarks the evaluation mechanism. The argument does not validate every comfortable preference, replace evidence or risk controls, or resolve institutional needs for coordination and quality standards. It remains a short persuasive essay with no comparative outcomes or fit-measurement method, and the saved page displays no byline. The Markdown contains no image references, so no visual asset or manifest was required.

The newest Google Search Console source adds [[SEOConsultantSelection]] as a governed vendor decision rather than a purchasable ranking promise. The proposed sequence is to learn enough SEO basics to recognize discouraged methods, test a consultant's relevant work, techniques, references, expected timeframe, measurement, communication, and understanding of the business, then commission a technical and search audit with read-only [[GoogleSearchConsole|Search Console]] access before granting implementation authority. [[Google]] explicitly separates organic ranking from advertising and places responsibility for consultant-made changes on the site owner, strengthening [[FailureInformedVendorSelection]] with staged permissions, corroboration, and change visibility. Guaranteed first place, secrecy, privileged-submission claims, shadow domains, doorway pages, hidden cross-client links, link schemes, fake search traffic, aliases, and disguised ad spend are rejection signals because they transfer control or platform-policy risk without a credible outcome guarantee. The evidence remains platform-authored guidance rather than comparative hiring research: the four-month-to-one-year result window is a broad heuristic, and legacy terminology and links in the saved page require current operational details to be rechecked. The Markdown contains no image references, so no visual asset or manifest was required.

The newest [[MattDay]] source adds [[VoiceApplicationMarketplace]] as the economic consequence of the wiki's existing voice-interface limits. By March 2019 [[AmazonEcho]] had reached broad consumer adoption and Alexa offered roughly 80,000 Skills, yet use remained concentrated in music, timers, weather, news, and smart-home control; half of surveyed smart-speaker users reportedly did not seek out applications, and interviewed developers could not identify a voice-native runaway hit. This turns [[VoiceAssistantUX]] discoverability into an ecosystem test: users must know a capability exists, remember how to invoke it, and prefer speech to a phone before catalog supply can become habitual demand. Amazon email, spoken prompts, companion-app listings, launch promotion, and best-of placement made discovery platform-mediated, while subscriptions, a 30% platform share, restricted advertising, content costs, and opaque developer rewards left sustainability uncertain. The durable distinction is between application count and marketplace health; the evidence remains a 2019 snapshot based on ten developer interviews, company claims, and third-party surveys, without retention cohorts, complete revenue distributions, audited subsidies, or later outcomes. All three local images were opened and omitted as an editorial Echo photograph and two low-resolution portraits that added no evidence beyond the prose.

The newest private-cloud source adds [[PrivateCloudStrategy]] as the sequencing and capability boundary inside [[EnterpriseCloudMigration]]. Its argument is that building compute, storage, networking, fault domains, load balancing, DNS, and failover on owned infrastructure can consume years before an enterprise migrates stateless applications, confronts stateful monoliths, or changes its operating model; an improved data center can therefore become a local optimum rather than progress toward the intended destination. The essay also broadens cost from server-versus-VM prices to engineering, network automation, procurement delay, agility, resilience, and forgone business work, and connects ticket-driven infrastructure to centralized coordination while programmable self-service can support team autonomy. The useful synthesis is conditional rather than categorical: private or hybrid capacity can be rational for regulation, sovereignty, latency, disconnected operation, specialized hardware, predictable utilization, sunk assets, or migration safety, but it needs an explicit advantage, scope, destination, and retirement test. The 200,000- and 1,000-server boundaries, near-universal public-cloud coverage, TLS timing, and cultural effects remain unverified 2016 practitioner claims. Of five local embeds, three were duplicate versions of one conceptual server-count chart and the highest-resolution copy was retained; two other files were too degraded at 60×31 and 60×4 pixels to interpret, so the source is not claimed as a complete visual ingest.

The newest [[AndreasKlinger]] source adds [[EmailTaskManagement]] as a small explicit-state system rather than an attempt to complete every obligation inside the inbox. Its historical [[Gmail]] implementation maps special stars to action, awaiting-reply, delegated, and scheduled states, surfaces those states through search-backed side panels, archives processed threads, and lets new replies return to the inbox. Filters, unsubscribe decisions, shortcuts, auto-advance, undo send, and account consolidation reduce handling overhead around that loop. [[blog-jeff-huang-my-productivity-app-is-a-never-ending-txt-file]] supplies an important cross-source qualification: Huang also uses immediate, eventual, and awaited-reply flags but integrates selected work into a bounded daily plan and does not center inbox zero. The durable synthesis is therefore explicit state plus consistent review; an empty inbox is optional and can conceal unfinished work if its saved views are not maintained. All 15 unique screenshots were inspected and retained because they document the concrete interface, queries, state symbols, filters, processing controls, and account settings; the repeated overview embed was collapsed to one canonical copy. The screenshots show an older Gmail interface, including Labs-era controls, so they are historical evidence rather than current configuration instructions.

The newest [[PaulNewson]] source adds [[IncidentManagement]] as the coordination layer joining the wiki's preventive and recovery-oriented reliability controls. In the [[GoogleComputeEngine]] case, general and service-specific training, scenario drills, shadowing, secondary duty, and access to an experienced responder prepared the first-time primary without treating on-call as solitary expertise. Potential impact, scope, and complexity triggered formal declaration; command, operations, assistance, and external communication roles then worked from a central incident record. [[ChangeSafety]] supplied the mitigation path because progressive rollout kept the release-related fault relatively limited and a known, tested rollback restored service. New [[BlamelessPostmortem]] extends the loop beyond closure: system-focused review produced nine owned actions, while a common template and weekly review supported recurring-cause analysis and shared learning. The account strengthens [[SystemReliability]] and [[IncidentCommunication]] but remains a company-published 2017 success case without impact measures, detailed root cause, comparative outcomes, or follow-up completion. Its only effective saved image was a generic Google Cloud social-card URL that now returns HTTP 404, so it could not be inspected and no visual evidence was retained.

The newest Ben Schippers source adds an incentive mechanism to the wiki's product-simplicity material. Engineering exploration rewards breadth, flexibility, and demonstrations of what a system can do, while product design must frame what people need, choose what the product should do, and remove the rest. This strengthens [[BuilderUserFluencyGap]] beyond knowledge asymmetry: builders can value exposed controls because technical possibility is intrinsically and socially rewarding even when users experience the same flexibility as decision pressure. [[CognitiveOverheadInProductDesign]], [[UserCenteredDesign]], and [[UtilityOrientedUX]] therefore converge on purposeful subtraction, but not minimalism as an end. Configurability, accessibility, safety, expert workflows, explanation, and recovery remain legitimate when grounded in user evidence or progressively disclosed. The article is a short 2015 practitioner argument that generalizes about engineers without comparative teams, user research, or product outcomes. Its two remote embeds resolve to one decorative green Uglydoll photograph, which was inspected and omitted without an asset manifest.

The newest [[EricFu]] source adds [[TimeSeriesDatabase]] as a data-model distinction rather than a market label. A series is a timestamp-value vector identified by a metric or table name plus labels; the same collection can be viewed as whole vectors selected by name and labels or as relational-like snapshots repeated at each query time. That duality separates time-axis aggregation, which can resample one series and require gap filling, from label-axis aggregation, which combines several aligned series without changing the timestamp vector; interval rounding and as-of matching address joins between independently sampled clocks. [[Prometheus]] anchors the snapshot-oriented query view, while [[InfluxDB]] anchors the vector view; [[GreptimeDB]] and [[TDengine]] add LSM-Parquet and supertable variants. The author's exclusion of [[TimescaleDB]] and [[QuestDB]] from the narrow category is a taxonomy choice, not a denial that they serve temporal workloads. This sharpens [[DatabaseConsolidation]]: vector-native storage and operators can justify specialization when data truly has stable name-label series, whereas timestamped relational rows alone do not. Six explanatory diagrams were retained at their semantic positions; the decorative cover was omitted. The product comparison contains no benchmarks, and GreptimeDB's performance rationale is explicitly speculative.

The newest [[BrianRJackson]] source turns time-series abstractions into a personal, cross-layer project. A WS2032 broadcasts weather observations at 433 MHz; an RTL-SDR and [[Rtl433]] decode them; MQTT and [[HomeAssistant]] discover, name, convert, and forward the entities; [[InfluxDB]] retains history; and [[Grafana]] applies Flux windows, pivots, filters, quantiles, mappings, thresholds, plugins, and overrides. New [[PersonalTelemetryPipeline]] treats acquisition, messaging, semantic normalization, storage, analysis, and presentation as separate but inspectable stages. The retained architecture diagram makes those boundaries explicit, while a dashboard overview, wind rose, speed heatmap, and direction-percentile view show why one chart cannot answer every question about noisy data. The case also adds analytical limits to [[TimeSeriesDatabase]] and Grafana: exact post-window alignment can discard unmatched observations, linear percentiles can misrepresent circular direction around 0/360 degrees, and attractive panels do not establish sensor accuracy or query validity. One code comment reverses the km/h-to-mph conversion description, a later heatmap uses a rougher coefficient, and the single historical hobby deployment supplies no reliability, security, recovery, retention, or product-comparison evidence. All 21 local images were opened; five evidence-bearing views were retained and installation, setup, card, and repeated dashboard images were omitted.

The newest [[Loish]] source adds [[ArtBlock]] as a visual-art instance of [[CreatorAnxiety]] and extends [[ProlificPractice]] with retrospective self-comparison. Paired 2004 and 2016 drawings visibly differ in anatomy, volume, gesture, detail, and line confidence, making a creator's own earlier work a more informative progress baseline than current flaws judged only against professionals. The practical response combines evidence and reduced stakes: revisit old work to notice development, then allow the next attempt to be poor or playful so fear of failure does not prevent making. This also connects to [[CreativePresence]], because drawing for enjoyment can loosen performance pressure. The evidence remains selected before-and-after work plus practitioner testimony; it does not isolate repetition from instruction, feedback, maturation, elapsed time, or curation, and it does not address every cause of persistent creative blockage. Two unique comparison images were retained at their semantic positions, while a lower-resolution duplicate of the portrait comparison was omitted.

The newest [[MorganHousel]] source adds [[KnowledgeDurability]] as a time-horizon filter for reading and judgment. Recent acquisitions, quarterly results, vacancy rates, and one-year manager performance may be useful now, but their value decays unless they are interpreted through recurring mechanisms such as industry consolidation, sustainable competitive advantage, demand drivers, motivation, and execution. This extends [[MentalModels]] by showing how durable causal frameworks can organize later observations and combine with ideas from other domains; it also qualifies [[InformationOverload]] and [[FocusedReading]] by making likely future relevance one selection criterion. The synthesis is complementary rather than anti-news: current facts show what happened, while longer-lived explanations help decide what deserves attention and what it means. The article offers examples and personal recall rather than measured evidence of retention, transfer, or decision quality; books can contain obsolete detail, journalism can reveal durable mechanisms, and apparently timeless models still need testing against change. The remote lead image returned 404 over HTTP and HTTPS, and the current publisher page exposes no replacement, so no visual evidence was used.

The newest [[Pinterest]] source adds [[ContextualSignalCollection]] as a bridge between personalization data, product education, and onboarding design. [[SophiaFeng]] reports that asking Google-authenticated users for gender before registration improved activation among those who continued but reduced Google signups by 30%; moving a redesigned request after signup reportedly increased onboarding completion by 11% despite adding a step. A Facebook cohort with complete gender coverage also improved by 8%, suggesting that explaining how Pinterest personalizes content contributed separately from obtaining a missing field. This qualifies [[ProductFlowFriction]]: an extra action is not inherently harmful when it resolves uncertainty or teaches users why later value depends on setup, while a useful request can still fail when it violates the expected authentication boundary. The evidence is a first-party 2018 retrospective with relative metrics but no sample sizes, absolute rates, uncertainty, retention, or recommendation-quality outcomes. Its binary gender framing and coverage-first language also omit consent quality, privacy, inclusivity, fairness, non-disclosure, and whether less intrusive signals could provide comparable relevance. The retained control-flow diagram grounds the baseline transition from Google authentication through registration into topic selection and the home feed.

The newest [[BenThompson]] source adds [[AggregatorMonopolyPower]] as a side-specific account of harm in free, multi-sided platforms. [[Facebook]]'s near-zero marginal cost for another user weakens the conventional user-price and quantity test, but Thompson argues that demand control can still reduce publisher bargaining power, make constrained advertising inventory more profitable if prices rise, and let an incumbent copy [[Snapchat]]'s Stories format and camera-first vision into a much stronger network. This extends [[AggregationTheory]] from concentration and data processing into surplus allocation and innovation incentives, while [[PlatformPublisherRevenue]] and [[PlatformDistributionDependence]] show why content suppliers might keep participating despite weak native monetization. The synthesis remains source-scoped: this 2017 strategy essay does not define a legal market, observe the predicted ad-price response, estimate publisher counterfactual revenue, or measure innovations displaced by copying. Its sole effective local image was opened and retained as a diagram of Facebook capturing most innovation benefit while leaving reduced consumer benefit and deadweight loss; several earlier economic graphs mentioned in the prose were absent from the Markdown export.

The newest [[JonFingas]] source adds [[CompetitiveIntelligence]] as an information mechanism behind incumbent response. Aggregated app-frequency and duration data from [[Onavo]] Protect reportedly let [[Facebook]] see [[Snapchat]] slowing after Instagram Stories, assess [[WhatsApp]]'s geographic strength before acquiring it, and observe Meerkat and Periscope before adding live video. This extends [[DataFactories]] beyond recommendation and advertising: consumer telemetry can become strategic output that shortens the interval between a challenger's traction and an incumbent's decision to copy, buy, or enter. It also sharpens [[AggregatorMonopolyPower]], because network distribution and privileged rival visibility can reinforce one another. The evidence remains a 2017 Engadget summary of Wall Street Journal reporting with no raw data, sampling method, causal identification, or internal decision records. Facebook said collection and use were disclosed, but notice does not establish user comprehension or settle purpose compatibility, platform-policy, or competition concerns. The sole local image was opened and omitted as a generic Facebook editorial photograph without independent evidence.

The newest [[KurtGessler]] source adds a measured publisher case to [[PlatformDistributionDependence]] and [[AlgorithmicFeastAndFamine]]. For the [[ChicagoTribune]], Facebook posts reaching at most 10,000 people rose from 8 in December 2016 to 242 in March 2017—about one-third of posts—even as the page gained more than 130,000 fans. Daily average organic reach remained volatile but superficially familiar, while average per-post reach declined and the median reached a record low; this makes distribution buckets and medians better diagnostics than follower growth or aggregate averages when a few successes can conceal many severe misses. Posting rose from roughly 20 to 24 times daily and the page's 97.2% link mix was high, but both were broadly consistent with peer newspaper practice and the content mix had not materially changed. Facebook's nearby “authentic and timely” update, non-adoption of Instant Articles, news cycles, competition, post quality, and cadence remain possible explanations rather than established causes because the evidence is one publisher's observational time series without post-level controls or platform-side data. Two full-resolution charts were retained; seven 60×40 thumbnails were opened and omitted because their material information was repeated in prose and their labels were not reliably legible.

The newest FastNetMon source adds [[DDoSTrafficMonitoring]] as a staged operational pipeline rather than a single “ban” action. In its historical CentOS 7 example, [[FastNetMon]] scopes CIDR ranges, consumes packet or flow telemetry, evaluates packet-rate, bandwidth, and flow thresholds, invokes a callback, and exports Graphite-formatted measurements to [[InfluxDB]]; [[Grafana]] then combines direction-specific Mbps and packet rates with trends and top-talker tables. A deliberately low-threshold `iperf` UDP test verifies metric flow, detection state, and notification logging, but does not establish production accuracy, false-positive behavior, sustained capture capacity, or actual packet enforcement. This sharpens [[NetworkAutomation]] by placing BGP or FlowSpec mitigation behind an explicit integration boundary: the article discusses route-based diversion, yet its supplied ExaBGP and FlowSpec options are disabled and no mitigation or recovery is tested. The source is also version-bound to a 2019 stack, so its CentOS 7 commands, InfluxDB 1.7.6, Grafana 6.1.6, dashboard template, and FastNetMon syntax require current verification. The sole local image was opened and retained at its semantic position because it demonstrates the dashboard's gauges, directionality, time traces, refresh window, and ranked host tables.

The newest Outline source adds a listener-side discovery layer to the wiki's Spotify material. New [[MusicDiscovery]] treats discovery as a portfolio rather than a contest between algorithms and nostalgia: [[Spotify]] supplies related artists, friends' playlists, Discover, and Release Radar; [[Bandcamp]] exposes tags, collections, buyer trails, and editorial browsing; [[SoundCloud]] is presented as an early route into emerging hip-hop, rap, and trap; and friends, professional contacts, publications, submissions, shows, record stores, liner notes, and musical histories supply human context and branching paths. [[JenMalone]], [[LaurenRearick]], [[HuaHsu]], [[DrDemento]], [[DelaneyMotter]], and [[MarcusMoore]] differ in role, genre, access, age, and available time, but collectively distinguish encountering a track from developing deeper attachment to an artist or scene. The source is six selected 2018 self-reports, not comparative evidence that human curation is more diverse or effective than algorithms, and several speakers benefit from professional access unavailable to ordinary listeners. Its single local image was opened and omitted as a decorative stock composition with no source-specific evidence.

The newest [[ZachHolman]] source adds [[EmployeeTermination]] as an end-to-end organizational process rather than a slogan about firing speed. His attributed 2015 [[GitHub]] experience connects warning and good-faith performance improvement, decision-making under shock, automated but dependency-aware access removal, truthful internal communication, written separation terms, severance, benefits, equity deadlines, coworker support, and alumni relationships. The source strengthens [[ExtendedStockOptionExerciseWindow]] by showing how a compressed exercise deadline and unclear prior expectations can create immediate financial pressure, while its “90 days by law” wording is not reliable universal legal or tax guidance. Holman's case also qualifies categorical rejection of performance improvement plans in [[ManagerialResponsibility]] and [[CompassionateManagement]]: a sham plan can be cruel, but a genuine process can clarify expectations, permit response, constrain bias, and reduce surprise. The evidence remains a retrospective U.S. startup account whose dismissal rationale was unresolved and whose legal, HR, benefits, and tax claims are jurisdiction-specific. Five referenced local images could not be inspected because the supplied asset directory is absent.

The newest technical-leadership source adds a compact pre-commitment review protocol for unfamiliar systems. [[TechnicalDecisionReview]] asks five linked questions: what the team is doing and why, how it could fail, how failure will be detected, what response is available, and whether the decision can be undone. This connects [[UnderstandDesignBuild]] to [[ServiceObservability]] and [[ChangeSafety]] by requiring purpose, assumptions, milestones or monitoring, recovery stakes, and reversibility to be discussed as one decision loop. It also sharpens [[TechnicalLeadershipRoleDesign]]: a lead can contribute through disciplined inquiry, comprehension, and action without pretending to be the deepest specialist, while the framework remains practitioner advice and does not replace domain expertise or prove that a nominal rollback restores distributed state.

The newest Vine essay sharpens the wiki's creator-platform synthesis by treating creator audiences as fragmented and partly portable rather than automatically locked into one social graph. [[Vine]] could mint prominent creators and command cultural attention, yet leading creators moved on as growth stagnated and monetization remained difficult. This broadens the [[CreatorGraduationProblem]] beyond creators building independent stacks or resisting take rates: creators can also graduate by reallocating effort toward another network that offers better economics. Audience creation is therefore only one retention input; durable creator platforms also need monetization, differentiated tools, demand, community, or other value that survives cross-platform switching. The source is a brief contemporary argument without comparative data, so it does not establish how much monetization caused Vine's decline relative to competition, product strategy, governance, or other factors.

The newest [[SamGerstenzang]] source adds [[StartupBoardGovernance]] as a balance between founder operating context and director accountability. Founders usually possess more detailed company and market information, while experienced directors may contribute cross-company pattern recognition, standards for unfamiliar executive roles, and independence when performance or conduct threatens the company. This extends [[FounderInvestorFit]] from chemistry, speed, services, and post-close burden into board philosophy: respecting founder judgment is different from promising unconditional founder loyalty. It also adds a succession boundary to [[CEOScalingRole]], because the leader suited to discovery and product-market fit may not be suited to incentive design, organizational scale, or multi-product expansion. The source distinguishes formal evaluation from confidential coaching, but it remains one normative practitioner essay. It supplies no comparative outcome evidence, does not resolve who defines the company's interests, and does not protect against directors mistaking investor preference or faulty pattern matching for warranted intervention. Its Plaxo, Facebook, Benchmark, and Uber references are incomplete illustrations, and its claim that earlier Benchmark action would have improved Uber is counterfactual. The supplied Markdown contains no effective image references.

The newest Chrome retrospective adds a two-sided history of [[Chrome]] and creates [[BrowserPlatformStrategy]]. The article attributes Chrome's rise from a cited 0.3% share in 2008 to almost 70% in May 2019 to clean-slate multi-process architecture, speed, Chromium, extensions, mobile reach, and enterprise tooling; its images make process isolation, extension governance, and later platform expansion explicit. The same compounding loop made Chrome a de facto implementation target, narrowed independent engine diversity after Edge adopted Chromium, and turned browser/Google identity integration into a privacy boundary. This strengthens [[WebCentralization]] by showing how a useful product and developer ecosystem can become infrastructure influence without treating dominance as proof that every standards decision is abusive. The source remains a secondary 2019 retrospective with provider-dependent share figures and chronology errors, so its causal account and measurements are source-scoped.

The newest Fortune feature adds a contemporary 2016 account of [[DeepLearning]]'s commercial inflection point. It joins old [[NeuralNetwork]] and [[Backpropagation]] ideas to [[ImageNet]]'s labeled data, GPU acceleration from [[Nvidia]], internet-scale speech and image corpora, open software, cloud access, and conspicuous results in recognition. [[GeoffreyHinton]], [[YannLeCun]], [[FeiFeiLi]], and [[AndrewNg]] connect the field's research lineage, datasets, and industrial strategy; [[UnsupervisedLearning]] captures the promise and ambiguity of the Google Brain cat experiment; and [[AlphaGo]] extends the story through [[ReinforcementLearning]] and self-play. The source also supplies its own boundary: strong pattern recognition was not broad reasoning, and 2016 startup, medical, funding, efficiency, and corporate-adoption claims were attributed snapshots rather than proof of clinical validity, open-world robustness, or general intelligence. Its two local images were opened and omitted as duplicate, non-evidentiary conceptual illustrations.

The newest [[JonathanCourtney]] source adds [[RemoteDesignSprint]] through [[AJSmart]]'s cross-continental redesign of [[Oak]] with founder [[KevinRose]]. Familiar [[DesignSprint]] moves—expert interview, “How Might We” notes, goal and questions, mapping, lightning demos, sketches, voting, and prototyping—were carried through a shared RealtimeBoard, unusually explicit notes, client inspiration examples, narrated feedback, prototype variants, and additional check-ins. The case makes staged alignment concrete: the team reduced direction uncertainty before full production and used [[Figma]] plus Marvel to turn a selected Japanese-influenced watercolor direction into screen designs. It also sharpens the method's evidence boundary. The brief grew from one screen to a total redesign, handoff took four weeks, and the article reports client buy-in, App Store featuring, and Product Hunt recognition without representative-user testing, baseline metrics, retention, or causal evidence that the process produced those outcomes. All six embedded images were opened; the high-resolution Oak interface and Product Hunt badge were retained, while two duplicate thumbnails, one tiny launch screenshot, and an author photo were omitted as duplicate, too low-resolution, or decorative.

The newest [[MathildeCollin]] source adds a firsthand founder-side layer to [[StartupFundingRound]] and resolves the underlying account behind the wiki's earlier [[Front]] retention case. Collin says Front waited until $100,000 in MRR, low churn, and a clear roadmap, then shifted decisively into fundraising: she spent about 90% of her workdays on the deck, data, projections, and feedback, received three term sheets in ten days, accepted one, and stopped meetings because the 15-person company's productivity loss was visible. Advance investor relationships mattered because the Series A lead would become the first board member, while selective disclosure mattered because investors continuously collect company, market, and competitor signals. The deck's strongest evidence was spending below ARR and a [[SaaSLandAndExpand]] result of customers spending 50% more after 12 months net of churn. Its weak or missing evidence—scalable acquisition channels, a capital-deployment model, engagement measures including [[DAUMAU]], and a defined buyer—shows that traction alone does not answer how new capital will produce repeatable growth. The metrics and process outcomes remain founder-reported snapshots without cohort definitions, audited financials, deal terms, valuation, or investor perspectives; the unusually fast successful process is an example, not a benchmark. The supplied Markdown contains no effective image references.

The newest [[SimonParkin]] source adds [[GameIndustryLaborPrecarity]] as a systems account of why creative game careers can become unsustainable. [[FrankDAngelo]]'s repeated short contracts, four interstate moves in five years, rapid post-relocation layoff, depleted savings, and eventual move into finance connect project churn to household risk. [[JAllard]] supplies the production mechanism: fluid scope, technology and platform shifts, holiday deadlines, optimistic forecasts, publisher budget pressure, and continuing servers, patches, downloadable content, cheating, and monetization work transfer uncertainty into understaffing and crunch. [[RickKelly]] shows that [[IndieGameDevelopment]] can restore ownership without guaranteeing livelihood even after visible store rankings, while [[AlejandroScrivano]] adds cross-functional strain and an alleged investor theft that closed a studio. [[KristenKoster]] extends [[WorkplaceSexismInTech]] through credibility denial, design-role displacement after her husband's promotion, a caregiving-incompatible support offer, and extreme on-call expectations. The article's 2018 GDC tenure figures are suggestive rather than causal: conference attendance is not a representative workforce panel, and the selected exit narratives do not establish prevalence. Its structural alternatives—moving staff among projects, internal tools, training, and prototypes—are proposals rather than measured remedies. The single local `.jpg` could not be interpreted or retained because its bytes are actually HTML rather than image data.

[[BenWeber]]'s 2016 [[StarCraft]] forecast sharpens the wiki's boundary between game milestones and more demanding decision environments. [[AlphaGo]] combined learned components, self-play, and search in a fully observable turn-based game; [[StarCraftAITestbed]] adds fog-of-war inference, control over many heterogeneous units, economic-to-tactical time horizons, evolving maps and counters, rare all-in strategies, limited simulation access, and real-time timing. The result also qualifies [[ReinforcementLearning]]: scalable experience generation is only one requirement, while state and action abstraction, opponent diversity, adaptation, and hybrid reactive control can determine whether the learned policy is usable. The source remains a 2016 proposal rather than evidence of a completed system, and the unavailable task-environment figure prevents a full cell-by-cell transcription of its comparison.

The newest [[GameBoy]] source connects launch-era product judgment with post-market cultural reuse. [[GunpeiYokoi]]'s [[LateralThinkingWithWitheredTechnology]] explains why [[Nintendo]] could accept weaker specifications when lower price, manageable battery needs, and true portability produced a better whole product. New [[HardwareAfterlives]] then separates restoration from selective transformation: enthusiasts replace shells, add backlights and audio hardware, turn the console into a synthesizer or MIDI-controlled instrument, and preserve the Game Boy Camera's 128-by-112-pixel monochrome limits as an aesthetic choice. [[Chiptune]] likewise becomes more than nostalgia, combining portable cartridge software, performance control, emotionally distinctive timbre, and local community formation. The evidence is a celebratory 2019 feature built from selected practitioners; its 110-million-unit figure, best-selling claim, broad mobile-gaming influence, and continuity with the Switch remain source-scoped rather than independently established. The retained photograph directly illustrates intimate handheld use but does not prove the article's market claims.

The newest [[GibsonBiddle]] source adds [[BrandPositioning]] and the [[BrandPyramid]] as complementary direction-setting tools inside [[StartupBrandStrategy]]. Positioning asks what a product is, how it benefits customers, and what relational personality it should express; the pyramid then connects changing product attributes to functional benefits, emotional benefits, and a long-term aspiration. [[Netflix]] supplies the historical case: DVD selection, queues, no late fees, streaming reach, and original content changed while easy movie enjoyment, delight, and escape remained comparatively stable, and product and marketing repeatedly tested how to present the evolving offer. This extends [[BrandEquity]] with recognition, reduced explanation, trust, and willingness to pay as possible commercial expressions, while keeping causality narrow. Homepage A/B tests can estimate how tested presentations affect trial starts and free-to-paid conversion, but cannot isolate durable brand meaning from product quality, catalog, price, distribution, familiarity, or market structure; the reported 2% and 90% benchmarks also lack sample periods, segmentation, and uncertainty. Qwikster's reported 800,000 quarterly cancellations shows that accumulated trust can be impaired. The account is a selected former-executive retrospective, and all four local images were opened and omitted because they depict an event portrait, a “Customer Obsession” graphic, Starbucks Reserve artwork, and the Netflix logo rather than the positioning or pyramid diagrams named by the surrounding prose.

The newest [[AlexisRichardson]] source establishes [[GitOps]] as a closed operational loop rather than merely storing Kubernetes YAML in Git. At [[Weaveworks]], pull requests and pipelines changed versioned declarative intent; kubediff, ansiblediff, and terradiff compared that intent with development and production; alerts exposed persistent divergence; and [[WeaveFlux]] synchronized Git-managed definitions with clusters. This extends [[DeclarativeInfrastructure]] by distinguishing authoritative intended state from observable live state, and it adds a repository-driven operating role to [[Kubernetes]]. The reported reconstruction of deleted AWS services, clusters, applications, and observability in under 45 minutes illustrates how versioned definitions can improve recovery, but it is a single company-authored case tied to related products. Git rollback is also bounded: reverting a declaration cannot by itself reverse database changes, external effects, lost data, or a bad desired state that automation has faithfully propagated.

The newest [[FarnamStreet]] source adds [[ReversibleDecisionMaking]] as proportional process rather than a generic command to move fast. Its synthesis of [[JeffBezos]]'s one-way and two-way doors says genuinely reversible choices can proceed with incomplete information because action produces evidence and course correction remains available, while irreversible or nearly irreversible choices need slower analysis and consultation. This deepens [[MultiplePathsToYes]] by supplying the learning rationale behind decentralized experimentation and adds a reported 70% information threshold plus Amazon's 111-day one-hour-delivery case. The boundary is classification: technical rollback does not erase lasting safety, data, financial, trust, employee, customer, or third-party effects, and the source offers no measured optimum or reliable test for distinguishing the door types. Its second-hand medical example is not clinical guidance. The local diagram was inspected and retained as a circular two-way path beside a one-way arrow; the original remote lead image returned 404, while a surviving low-resolution republication showed only a decorative broken-versus-intact vase illustration and was omitted.

The newest [[MitchellHarper]] source adds a compact focus test to [[CEOScalingRole]], attributed to [[FredWilson]]: set and repeatedly communicate vision and strategy, recruit and retain exceptional talent, and preserve enough cash. The three responsibilities reinforce one another. Company-wide explanation connects purpose and individual roles to strategy; personal CEO involvement can help close critical candidates; and adverse-case runway protects the time needed to execute. [[ExecutiveHiring]] gains advance capacity planning, person-over-resume judgment, and near-term stage fit, while [[StartupRunway]] gains a downside-planning boundary and small-budget channel tests before aggressive spend. These are practitioner heuristics rather than validated thresholds: the annual strategy-change limit, two-quarter recruiting lead, 18-month candidate and runway horizons, and suggested three-times channel return may vary by business model and measurement method. Harper's assertion that the CEO understands the market best also needs customer evidence, distributed expertise, dissent, and governance checks. The inspected LEGO image and duplicated tiny book promotion were omitted as non-evidentiary.

The newest [[JustinBauer]] source broadens [[ModernProductTeamDesign]] from five structural conditions into an operating loop. At [[Amplitude]], Bauer argues that product management, design, and engineering should share direct customer context and behavioral evidence; a clear strategy and small set of important measures then let the team choose solutions, test risky assumptions through coherent incremental releases, and judge the result through engagement, stickiness, retention, customer outcomes, and revenue connection rather than story points or feature count. This strengthens [[CrossFunctionalProductTeams]], [[CustomerLedProductDevelopment]], [[IterativeProductShipping]], and [[ProductMetricLadder]] while preserving a critical boundary: analytics should inform judgment, not validate predetermined choices or replace vision. The sharp good-team/bad-team contrast is a practitioner diagnostic, not a comparative study; direct feedback and usage data can both be unrepresentative, high-consequence work may justify slower review, and Bauer's product-analytics employer gives the prescription a visible commercial context. The sole remote title image returned HTTP 404, no recoverable copy was located, and no image-derived claim was used.

The Wildbit product-management source strengthens the wiki's product operating model by making the team's working conditions part of product quality rather than a separate people concern. [[ProductManagement]] now combines direct customer access with a refusal to treat requested features as roadmap instructions, and it treats strategy as the distillation of customer, business, technology, and whole-team knowledge rather than the PM's personal idea supply. [[ModernProductTeamDesign]] gains sustainable pace, internal motivation, realistic capacity, process feedback, and hands-on obstacle removal as conditions around strategic autonomy and outcome accountability. [[ProductManagerAsCEO]] is correspondingly narrower: CEO language survives only when it communicates broad responsibility without status, command, overtime pressure, or distrust. [[ProductRetrospectives]] connect the two levels by pairing formal reflection with informal feedback about projects, iterations, and process. The account remains a one-company practitioner prescription without comparative outcome evidence, precise happiness measures, or complete guidance for emergencies and high-consequence work; all seven unique local illustrations were inspected and omitted as decorative or duplicated.

The newest [[CaseyWinters]] source adds [[SearchPlatformDisintermediation]] as a search-specific form of [[PlatformDistributionDependence]]. Its 2018 thesis is that mobile users' preference for immediate answers and compact options pushes [[Google]] from sending demand to third-party category pages toward owning more of discovery through direct answers, vertical cards, and build-buy-partner entry. For aggregators, internal-search and doorway-page rules can narrow the indexable inventory surface while listing-level participation preserves visibility at the cost of customer-interface control; the durable defense remains differentiated value, direct audience loyalty, and switching costs. This sharpens [[AggregationTheory]] because a platform controlling demand can absorb the specialized aggregator between itself and suppliers, but it does not establish a universal or completed transition. The source gives no cross-category traffic, conversion, or welfare measurements; its Chrome-data claim is unsupported, its AMP advice is historically situated, and an appended reader comment argues that specialist result pages can add comparison value and convert better than individual listings. The retained mobile screenshot provides source-specific evidence of Google presenting quinoa-recipe cards directly in search.

The newest [[RonAmadeo]] source adds [[ProductLifecycleTrust]] as the confidence that a product and its supporting services will persist long enough to justify adoption costs. Its April 2019 Google case connects shutdowns to different forms of dependency: consumers entrust data, purchased hardware, and social coordination; enterprises alter workflows; developers learn APIs and build applications; and manufacturers commit to multi-year design and support cycles. Repeated closures can therefore create portfolio-wide spillover, forcing an unrelated new team to answer for earlier decisions. [[GoogleStadia]] makes the mechanism concrete because launch reporting asked about service longevity alongside technical feasibility and appeal, while [[PhilHarrison]] acknowledged the concern and cited significant cross-company investment. That assurance is incomplete when previously well-funded products also closed. The source broadens [[DeveloperPlatformTrust]] to pricing, enforcement, recourse, and whole-product continuity, but it is an opinion analysis rather than a brand, adoption, or retention study; it groups unlike shutdowns, does not judge every closure's rationale, and records launch-time expectations rather than later Stadia outcomes. Two decorative Google-wordmark images were omitted, while one copy each of the duplicated discontinued-app strip and Stadia presentation photograph was retained.

The newest Rands in Repose source adds [[StaffMeetings]] as a conditional coordination system rather than a default calendar ritual. Team size, interdependence, management layers, rapid growth, recurring communication failures, or organizational disruption can justify a forum, but its continuing value depends on separate runner and historian roles, question-producing metrics, a team-owned rolling agenda, candid error correction, actionable follow-up, and notes shared beyond the room after necessary redaction. This qualifies the meeting-deletion critique in [[ProceduralRationality]]: a recurring meeting can remain substantive when its need, work, and outputs are visible and repeatedly reassessed, while uninformative metrics, empty agendas, or a vanished founding reason are signals to stop. Broad notes can reduce status games and speculative narratives, but they may also suppress candor or expose sensitive information; a designated rumor segment does not itself create [[PsychologicalSafety]], and the source's participant-count, duration, and timing heuristics are practitioner prescriptions rather than measured thresholds. The supplied Markdown contains no effective image references.

The newest [[TimOReilly]] source broadens [[LongNoseInnovation]] from product histories into a cross-domain attention heuristic: algorithmic coordination, mobile payments, drone logistics, precision agriculture, genomics, neural interfaces, embedded learning, climate response, and government capability can become suddenly consequential only after capabilities, infrastructure, and practice accumulate gradually. It also expands [[AugmentedIntelligence]] beyond decision support and activity redesign. Platform firms already operate as human-machine hybrids; CTRL-labs' nerve-signal demonstration suggests interfaces can add controllable virtual capability, while ride-hailing guidance illustrates performance-adjacent learning embedded in work. This is a normative and exploratory 2019 survey, not comparative outcome evidence or a timing model: numerical examples are historical snapshots, several forecasts are untested here, the saved Africa and economics passages are incomplete, and augmentation can conceal allocation power, surveillance, and coordination pressure unless authority and recourse remain explicit. The sole local image was opened and omitted as a decorative ocean-sunrise photograph.

The newest Know Your Meme source adds [[GreaterInternetFuckwadTheory]] as a durable internet-culture shorthand rather than a validated behavioral law. [[PennyArcade]]'s 2004 chalkboard equation joins an ordinary person, anonymity, and an audience to explain abusive conduct, while the article's 1978 CB-radio precursor suggests that reduced accountability can matter outside the internet. [[JohnSuler]]'s [[OnlineDisinhibitionEffect]] supplies the more useful mechanism boundary: anonymity is only one factor beside invisibility, asynchronicity, solipsistic introjection, dissociative imagination, minimized authority, personality differences, and altered self-boundaries, and lowered restraint can produce benign disclosure as well as toxic harassment. The source's selected YouTube, 4chan, gaming, misogyny, and racism examples establish cultural circulation, not prevalence or causality; they do not show that identity disclosure alone improves conduct. All nine local image files were opened, two duplicate originals were consolidated, and five evidence-bearing visuals were retained. The shared remote GIF URL identifies itself as a blank placeholder but could not be fetched because its host did not resolve; every remote reference had a cached local original that was inspected.

The newest [[GregBrockman]] source adds OpenAI's 2015-2017 formation and early research infrastructure to the wiki's later product-and-governance view of [[OpenAI]]. Brockman's central organizational claim is constraint-driven: he first recruited, organized, and removed non-research work from [[IlyaSutskever]], then exchanged responsibilities with him when [[OpenAIGym]] software became the bottleneck, and later argued that a roughly forty-person research organization needed full-time organizational execution. This qualifies a one-way reading of [[StartupCTORoleEvolution]] and [[TechnicalLeadershipRoleDesign]]: senior technical attention can move back into hands-on implementation when engineering limits discovery, provided ownership is explicit. New [[MachineLearningResearchEngineering]] names the software boundary around the algorithmic core - data movement, interfaces, metrics, video, distributed scheduling, and experiment orchestration - while Gym and [[OpenAIUniverse]] show why researcher workflow and iteration latency are part of research design. The source remains a January 2017 founder retrospective: it does not independently verify causal credit, recruiting perspectives, project outcomes, or the sustainability of intense coding, and its cooperative-AI vision is an aspiration rather than a demonstrated result. The supplied Markdown contains no effective image references.

The newest [[EvWilliams]] source adds a concurrent working-parent model to [[WorkLifeBalance]] alongside the wiki's existing life-course account. In Williams's selected network of successful parents, 55-60 focused hours was the largest band, only 2% reported 90 or more hours, and most respondents did some weekend work, usually in a limited block. Founders reported more work outside the office, while longer hours were more common at larger and older companies. The strongest structural signal is household support: 73% reported childcare assistance, including 77% of founders, making care arrangements part of the workload story rather than invisible background. These figures challenge a simple 100-hour startup myth but cannot replace it with a 55-60-hour norm. The article omits its sample size and response denominator, draws mostly from a founder-heavy technology network, had too few women for gender analysis, and provides no causal, health, family, or company-outcome evidence. Both local images were opened; the full-size family-skiing photograph repeated the closing anecdote and its second occurrence was a thumbnail duplicate, so neither was retained.

The newest Netflix TechBlog source adds [[GrowthEngineering]] as a joint product, experimentation, and platform discipline. Its signup funnel keeps landing, plan selection, registration, and payment as broad stages while allowing device input, market expectations, partner billing, browser capabilities, and local payment methods to alter the actual path. [[ConversionRateOptimization]] therefore expands from isolated page or form tactics into an end-to-end system whose tests depend on shared business logic, trustworthy event collection, downstream metrics, and reliable execution. [[MicroservicePlatformEngineering]] gains a client-facing pattern: lightweight applications consume a small stateless JSON protocol while an orchestration service validates and enriches requests, invokes a state machine, coordinates downstream services, and composes the next response. The source says Netflix experiments constantly and targets conversion, retention, revenue, and experience, but provides no experiment samples, effects, reliability measurements, or comparative architecture results. The two full-size evidence-bearing images were retained for the demand-to-viewing funnel and contrasting market/device flows; six 46-60-pixel decorative, duplicative, prose-repeated, or unreadable thumbnails were omitted.

The newest [[AndrewChen]] source adds an early organizational and implementation layer to [[GrowthHacking]]. The “growth hacker” is a marketer-coder hybrid spanning acquisition judgment, experiments, landing pages, email delivery, instrumentation, database work, and product engineering rather than a detached campaign role. [[Airbnb]]'s Craigslist integration makes the mechanism concrete: the source says the team worked without a public API by reverse-engineering forms, regional codes, posting-state URLs, contact handling, and restricted HTML, then optimized completion, calls to action, destination pages, unique links, and tracking pixels. This deepens [[StartupDistributionStrategy]] because product-embedded acquisition includes technical feasibility, measurement, maintenance, and channel exposure, while sharpening [[PlatformDistributionDependence]] because an undocumented interface can create both rapid reach and policy or breakage risk. The case remains a 2012 retrospective without traffic, conversion, retention, engineering-cost, platform-policy, or counterfactual evidence; its prediction that non-technical marketing leadership is fading is historically narrower than the hybrid-role label suggests. The supplied Markdown contains no effective image references.

The newest Threatpost source adds [[CodeSpaces]] as an extreme connection between cloud control-plane compromise, [[BackupAndRecovery]], and business continuity. The attacker reportedly combined a DDoS attack and extortion demand with [[AWS]] control-panel access, created persistent logins, and began deleting assets when recovery attempts were noticed. Direct machine access was unnecessary: EBS snapshots and volumes, S3 buckets, AMIs, instances, configurations, SVN repositories, and most backups were within the compromised administrative scope. This sharpens [[CloudAccountSegmentation]] because geographic distribution and nominally offsite copies do not provide recovery independence when one identity or account can delete them all. Code Spaces' advertised redundancy and reportedly practiced recovery plan therefore conflict with the outcome, which the company said made refunds, recovery cost, and lost credibility financially irreversible within about 12 hours. The evidence remains a 2014 secondary report based largely on Code Spaces' crisis statement; it does not establish initial access, independently verify the asset inventory, show which MFA or IAM controls were configured, or prove that account separation alone would have prevented the failure. The remote lead image was opened and omitted as a generic, non-evidentiary stock illustration.

The newest [[GaborSzathmari]] and [[JeremiahCruz]] source adds [[AbandonedDomainTakeover]] as a business-lifecycle failure that crosses domain registration, mail routing, account inventory, and recovery design. The authors report re-registering six selected former-business domains, operating catch-all email for three months, receiving about 25,000 messages, passing domain-ownership checks at breach services, and initiating resets across social, storage, legal, payment, advertising, and cloud systems. This extends [[AuthenticationInfrastructure]] across organizational time: proof of inbox control is only trustworthy while an authorized party retains the underlying domain and removes obsolete addresses from third-party accounts after mergers, rebrands, departures, or closure. MFA reportedly stopped an Office 365 recovery attempt, but it cannot prevent sensitive parties from continuing to send mail to a transferred namespace. The practical control set is layered—retain retired domains, close or update old accounts, notify correspondents, use unique passwords and MFA, and strengthen provider recovery flows. The evidence is a 2018 practitioner report using six hand-selected domains and roughly thirty credential subjects, not a prevalence study; the researchers say they stopped short of logging into recovered services, and almost all evidence screenshots in the supplied archive survive only as unreadable 50–60-pixel thumbnails.

The newest [[DanahBoyd]] source extends [[AttentionEconomy]] from a commercial incentive system into an adversarial arena for visibility and power. [[4chan]]'s ephemeral image-board design encouraged reposting and mutation, while coordinated participants learned to design memes for spread, game rankings and trends, trigger journalistic attention, and exploit ambiguity or in-group meaning. New [[NetworkedInformationManipulation]] joins those mechanics across playful trolling, marketing, activism, Anonymous, Gamergate, propaganda, and political organization without treating their motives or legitimacy as identical. The escalation matters: doxing, swatting, gaslighting, dog whistles, and distributed harassment can create reputational, psychological, economic, social, or physical harm, induce self-censorship, and seed doubt in institutions without depending on one explicit falsehood. The source's durable claim is that manipulation itself is not new, but networked tools increase accessible scale, coordination, ambiguity, and strategic use for acquiring power. Its evidence is one January 2017 interpretive history built from selected notorious cases; it does not quantify prevalence or effect, compare successful and failed campaigns, establish a simple causal descent among communities, or show that decentralized actors reliably control narratives. All four unique local images were opened and omitted: the lead “gun as megaphone” photograph and its tiny duplicate were decorative, while the tiny lolcat and Egypt/Facebook protest illustrations repeated examples already stated in prose.

The newest [[HappyXiao]] source adds emotional outcome detachment to the wiki's creator-practice model. Borrowing a [[MarcAndreessen]] anecdote about [[AndreessenHorowitz]] and professional gamblers, it argues that creators should make one piece after another, loosen each attempt's connection to applause or visible numbers, attend to their own growth, and play a longer game. This strengthens [[ProlificPractice]] by separating the repetition needed for learning from the emotional verdict attached to a single result, and it sharpens [[CreatorPlatformMetrics]] by distinguishing scheduled evidence review from compulsive reward-seeking. The useful synthesis is not to ignore data or suppress feeling: metrics can still reveal topic fit, packaging, distribution, and commercial outcomes, while persistent weak results can justify changing craft or strategy. The source is a very short personal essay built on a second-hand gambling analogy; it supplies no outcome evidence and does not establish that emotional suppression or risk-taking improves judgment. Its Markdown contains no image references, so no visual asset or manifest was required.

The newest [[MonikaBickert]] source adds [[PosthumousAccountGovernance]] as a multi-party extension of online identity. [[Facebook]]'s stated 2017 default was conservative continuity when a user's wishes were unknown: label the profile “Remembering,” block new logins, and preserve the content and audience boundaries the person left behind. Advance deletion preferences or a legacy contact could change that outcome, but the contact's enumerated powers did not amount to inheriting the identity or its private messages. This sharpens [[ContextCollapse]] because posthumous access can expose material beyond the audience chosen while the user was alive, and it adds living correspondents as independent privacy stakeholders even when a bereaved relative has a compelling reason to seek answers. Digital memory itself remains ambivalent: photographs, messages, and posts can support continued connection, while automated reminders and resurfaced material can renew grief. The evidence is a first-party policy explanation rather than a comparative or outcome study; preservation is still a substantive default, next-of-kin accounts of intent may be hard to verify, and the legal and product details are historical rather than current guidance. The recovered lead illustration was retained because it directly depicts the memorialized “Remembering” state; two decorative divider graphics were omitted.

The newest distributed-systems source establishes [[ServiceHealthChecks]] as decision-specific quality-of-service evidence rather than one binary status. A conservative liveness probe can support restart when a process crashes or deadlocks, while load balancing needs readiness, latency, queue, concurrency, correctness, and real-work capacity signals to avoid sending traffic to a reachable but overloaded backend. This extends [[NetworkLoadBalancing]] from packet paths and topology into runtime feedback, and extends [[DependencyDegradation]] from classifying weak dependencies into continuous partial-capacity control. New [[AdaptiveBackpressure]] names the resulting loop: workers admit or refuse work using local state, upstream components reroute or queue within bounds, saturated queues trigger rejection, and retry budgets plus backoff keep excess work from silently moving elsewhere. The historical [[Imgix]] case makes that loop concrete through [[Spillway]] worker selection, three dispatch attempts, LIFO/FIFO/priority queues, rejection, and [[Prometheus]] queue-depth alerts, while [[HAProxy]] agent checks show dynamic weight and connection-limit feedback. The account is a former employee's qualitative 2018 retrospective without comparative latency, throughput, loss, fairness, or recovery data; static bounds still matter, local control does not remove centralized rate limiting, and retries can amplify overload. All seven local images were opened: the full-resolution latency-variability whiteboard and four evidence-bearing thumbnails were retained, while one duplicate and one unreadable contextual graphic were omitted; fine labels and exact chart values were not inferred from 60-pixel-wide assets.

The newest [[HerbertLui]] source adds a year-long, roughly 800-card practitioner case to the wiki's [[ZettelkastenMethod]] cluster. The account makes regular review, not card accumulation, the operating mechanism: each new card creates an occasion to revisit older material, find a meaningful placement, and let article or book threads develop gradually. It also adds a lifecycle to [[NoteToolFit]] and [[PersonalKnowledgeManagement]]. Handwritten 4×6 cards initially provide focus, selection effort, and a hard length limit; digital transcription becomes valuable when physical identifiers and locations make retrieval too slow; and Markdown export supplies a practical exit criterion even when Notion is sometimes sluggish. Lui's willingness to omit a separate literature-note box and modify [[NiklasLuhmann]]'s model supports an adaptive rather than orthodox reading of the method. The evidence remains one self-reported 2021 retrospective: it does not compare outcomes against other workflows, and its memory, creativity, productivity, and interoperability claims are not independently established. All seven local images were opened; six evidence-bearing photographs or screenshots were retained under descriptive canonical filenames, while one redundant stack photograph was omitted.

The newest [[NicoleNguyen]] source adds [[AppPermissionGovernance]] as a continuing access decision rather than a one-time consent click. The 2017 [[UnrollMe]] case connects a useful inbox-cleanup feature and broad Google-account authority with a separate [[DataMonetization]] path: the article reports that receipt information extracted from email became an analytics product sold through Slice Intelligence to [[Uber]]. This sharpens the wiki's free-service model because targeted advertising, aggregate analytics, and transfer of derived records are distinct mechanisms even when each is compressed into “you are the product.” The practical loop is to compare requested capabilities with actual purpose, recognize that send/delete authority carries greater stakes than passive viewing, inspect privacy language and revenue sources, revisit connected apps and phone permissions, and revoke stale access. Terms summaries and paid alternatives may reduce review or incentive problems, but neither guarantees privacy, and [[PrivacyPovertyDivide]] qualifies the assumption that every user can afford to exit a data-funded service. The source is historical consumer journalism rather than a legal or technical audit: product policies and settings paths may have changed, the retained authorization screen proves requested scope rather than actual use of every capability, and the report does not test anonymization or reidentification. All four local images were opened; the full permission screen and TLDRLegal example were retained under descriptive filenames, while a duplicate crop and generic laptop photograph were omitted.

The newest [[RyanHoliday]] source adds the [[BriefcaseTechnique]] as a specific form of prepared opportunity use. Rather than treating an interview or high-value meeting as a passive question-and-answer session, the participant researches the recipient's problem and brings a diagnosis, proposed action, and implementation detail that make initiative and judgment inspectable. Nick Saban's legal pad, Andy Reid's accumulated coaching binder, and Holiday's account of an unnamed 26-year-old pitching [[PeterThiel]] show increasingly elaborate versions of the mechanism; the Thiel proposal also strengthens [[TechnologyElitePower]] by connecting private wealth to a shell company, investigators, lawyers, a multi-year timeline, and a large budget targeting [[Gawker]]. The durable synthesis is narrower than the article's successful examples: preparation can improve responsiveness when an opportunity appears, but it cannot guarantee selection, correct a misunderstood problem, or justify the objective ethically. The cases are retrospectively selected, Holiday supplies no success denominator, and escalating candidate-led preparation can create unpaid-work, access, and fairness burdens. The sole local image was opened and omitted as a decorative snowy-mountain landscape without article-specific evidence.

The newest [[BartoszGoralewicz]] source adds [[TechnicalSEO]] as a coupled discovery path rather than a collection of ranking tricks. In his 2018 [[GoogleFlights]] case, a client-rendered relaunch is said to combine inaccessible or unindexed content, blocked JavaScript, redirect chains, footer links, and inconsistent trailing-slash handling; SearchMetrics reportedly fell from about 20,000 to 47 and Sistrix reportedly showed the competing URL forms moving in opposite directions. This turns Google's own [[SEOConsultantSelection]] guidance back on a Google product: platform expertise and a visually improved interface do not ensure that a product team has verified crawler access, rendered output, canonical URL identity, direct redirects, internal-link priority, and index coverage. The durable measurement boundary is equally important. Visibility scores and rank checks can trigger investigation, but the article discloses no first-party analytics, logs, Search Console data, source code, Google confirmation, booking conversion, or revenue evidence, so its six-figure-loss framing and allocation of cause remain unverified. All five local images were opened; duplicate decorative airplane photographs and the author avatar were omitted, while the only potentially evidentiary comparison graphic was just 60 by 9 pixels and could not be read or retained.

The newest [[ArnoldSchwarzenegger]] source broadens [[LuckAndEffortInSuccess]] from starting conditions, judgment, preparation, and chance into the social infrastructure of achievement. Schwarzenegger retains agency—vision, work, and active mentor-seeking—but credits parents, teachers, coaches, temporary hosts, Reg Park, Joe Weider, Lucille Ball, and 4,206,284 California voters with supplying instruction, shelter, direction, sponsorship, career access, and collective political support that he did not create alone. This also deepens [[DeliberateNetworkBuilding]]: a formative network can include deliberately sought mentors and cross-domain heroes alongside unchosen family, freely offered help, gatekeepers, audiences, and institutions encountered across time. [[TimFerriss]] gains a bounded curatorial role through podcasts and *Tools of Titans*, which Schwarzenegger describes as channels for practical lessons from several fields. The durable conclusion is causal humility rather than passivity: acknowledging dependencies makes an attribution more complete and keeps learning open, but the autobiographical foreword does not measure each contribution or show that comparable help is equally available. Saved comments dispute whether “self-made” means literal solitude or self-directed advancement. All four historical Facebook CDN photographs returned HTTP 403, so their captions were used as prose but no visual detail was inferred or retained.

The newest [[KheHy]] source adds [[PersonalCRM]] as a relationship-retrieval system distinct from a commercial sales pipeline. Hy's Google Sheets implementation combines name and email with up to ten descriptors drawn from industry, job function, passions, and personal traits, then uses a controlled vocabulary, validation-backed typeahead, cell A1, and a named filter view to retrieve people for introductions, targeted information sharing, and events. This gives [[EndUserComputing]] a concrete data-oriented case: a non-specialist composes familiar spreadsheet primitives into a small personal database without conventional application code. The durable tradeoff is consistency versus expressiveness. Hard-coded tags reduce variants such as “Crossfit” and “Xfit,” while comments, domain-sensitive granularity, delayed tag promotion, and a free-form notes field preserve limited flexibility. The account remains one self-reported 2014 implementation of roughly 500 contacts; it does not measure retrieval quality, relationship depth, maintenance burden, privacy or security risk, or comparative outcomes, and a contact index does not establish that Dunbar-style cognitive limits have been surpassed. Seven local images were opened, six evidence-bearing taxonomy and workflow screenshots were retained, and one cropped duplicate was omitted. Two duplicate remote cover-image references returned HTTP 403 and could not be inspected, so no visual claim relies on them.

The newest [[KelseyPiper]] source extends [[HiringSystemDesign]] into [[CandidateRejectionFeedback]] and makes useful transparency conditional on process maturity. Piper reports that [[Triplebyte]] turned detailed multi-axis interviewer observations into individualized emails through central review, decision-relevant explanation, and maintained free learning resources, but reserved that effort for candidates who completed a two-hour interview. Candidate reactions reportedly improved when messages described what a person failed to demonstrate rather than declaring what they did not know, emphasized the sections that actually drove rejection, and made apparently mixed strengths and weaknesses more specific. The case therefore treats feedback as a downstream test of evidence quality and editorial governance: greater detail can intensify anger when it confirms misunderstanding, obscures causality, or appears contradictory. It also distinguishes reviewed technical-performance feedback from improvised release of raw notes that mention protected characteristics or expose bias, without establishing jurisdiction-independent legal safety. The evidence remains one employee's 2018 employer-published retrospective; more than 3,000 messages and mostly positive later reactions are self-reported without a corpus, response denominator, candidate survey, cost accounting, demographic analysis, complaint rate, comparison group, or downstream hiring outcomes. The source contains no image references, so no visual assets were inspected or retained.

The Tony Hsieh schedule analysis adds a management-and-productivity bridge between individual workflow and organizational information design. [[Yesterbox]] makes yesterday's inbox a bounded daily queue, but the [[TonyHsieh]] case also shows that high-volume executive email depends on delegation and chief-of-staff triage rather than individual discipline alone; [[EmailTaskManagement]] therefore needs explicit scope, ownership, urgency exceptions, and calendar capacity as well as flags or inbox-zero rituals. At the organizational level, [[OrganizationalTransparency]] treats shared priorities, calendars, decisions, and meeting records as infrastructure for decentralized judgment and fewer avoidable questions. [[Zappos]]'s 2015 Holacracy rollout is a suggestive but weak causal case: the article reports 54% fewer emails and 15% fewer daily work hours in selected year-over-year months, yet supplies no raw analysis and cannot separate transparency or Holacracy from delegation, staffing, seasonality, or other change.

The newest TechRepublic source makes the human production layer of AI visible through [[AmazonMechanicalTurk]].
